outputs.L3:
A component mounting positional deviation amount measurement unit is installed in the feeder setting section of a component mounting machine. The measurement unit is configured so that it can be exchanged with a cassette-type feeder, allowing it to be attached to or removed from the feeder setting section in the same manner as an ordinary feeder.

The measurement unit includes measurement nozzle placement sections, measurement component placement sections, and a measurement mounting table. The measurement mounting table is provided with a measurement fiducial mark that serves as a reference position for measuring mounting accuracy.

Measurement nozzles are exchangeably held by the mounting head of the component mounting machine. When not in use, the measurement nozzles are placed in the measurement nozzle placement sections of the measurement unit. The mounting head can pick up a selected measurement nozzle from these placement sections and use it for a measurement operation.

During measurement, the mounting head holds one of the measurement nozzles and moves to a measurement component placement section. The measurement nozzle then sucks and holds a measurement component. After that, the mounting head transfers the measurement component to the measurement mounting table and mounts it at a predetermined target position corresponding to the measurement fiducial mark.

After the measurement component has been mounted, the position of the mounted measurement component is compared with the position of the measurement fiducial mark on the measurement mounting table. The difference between the actual mounted position of the measurement component and the reference position indicated by the measurement fiducial mark is measured as the component mounting positional deviation amount. This measured deviation can be used to evaluate or correct the mounting accuracy of the component mounting machine.
outputs.L4:
An exchangeable measurement unit for a component mounting machine is installed in the feeder setting section of the machine in place of, or in addition to, an ordinary component feeder. This measurement unit is used to evaluate the mounting accuracy of the component mounting machine by detecting positional deviation that occurs when a component is picked up and mounted by the machine. The unit includes measurement nozzles, measurement components, and a mounting table provided with a fiducial mark that serves as a positional reference.

During measurement, the component mounting machine operates in substantially the same manner as it does during normal production. A mounting head of the machine picks up a measurement component using a measurement nozzle and transfers the component to the mounting table of the measurement unit. The mounting table has a fiducial mark whose position is known in advance. The machine then mounts the measurement component onto the table at a predetermined target position relative to the fiducial mark.

After the measurement component has been mounted, the position of the mounted component is compared with the position of the fiducial mark. This comparison may be performed by an imaging device, vision system, or other position-detecting means provided in the component mounting machine or in the measurement unit. Because the fiducial mark defines an accurate reference position, the difference between the detected position of the measurement component and the expected mounting position can be calculated as the mounting positional deviation of the machine.

The measured deviation may include displacement in the X direction and Y direction, as well as rotational deviation around the vertical axis. By analyzing these values, the system can determine whether the mounting head, nozzle, feeder setting section, transfer mechanism, or control parameters of the component mounting machine are properly aligned. If the detected deviation exceeds an allowable range, calibration data can be generated or corrected so that subsequent component mounting operations are performed with improved accuracy.

Since the measurement unit is exchangeable and can be installed in the feeder setting section, it can be used without requiring major modification of the component mounting machine. The measurement operation can be carried out periodically, during setup, after maintenance, or whenever mounting accuracy needs to be verified. This allows the machine’s placement performance to be evaluated under conditions close to actual mounting operation.

In this way, the exchangeable measurement unit provides a practical and accurate method for measuring component placement deviation. By mounting a measurement component onto a fiducial-marked mounting table and comparing the mounted position with the reference fiducial mark, the system enables precise calibration, inspection, and performance evaluation of the component mounting machine.

**When**

“When” is a small word, but it carries a great deal of meaning. It points to time, moments, choices, and change. We use it to ask about the future, remember the past, and understand the present.

When we are young, time often feels endless. Days seem long, and the future feels far away. As we grow older, we begin to understand how quickly moments pass. We learn that “when” is not just about a date or an hour—it is about opportunity.

When we choose to act, we create new possibilities. When we wait too long, chances may disappear. When we listen, we understand others better. When we make mistakes, we learn. Every “when” can become a turning point.

The word also reminds us that timing matters. The right words at the right time can comfort someone. A decision made at the right moment can change a life. Even patience has its own “when,” because some things need time to grow.

In the end, “when” is more than a question. It is a reminder that life happens in moments, and each moment has value. What matters most is not only what we do, but when we choose to do it.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention in this patent abstract about measuring component mounting positional deviation in a component mounting machine.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention concerns a way to measure how far a mounted component is displaced from its intended mounting position in a component mounting machine.

In essence, the machine captures image data of the mounted component and/or relevant board reference features, determines the actual position and orientation of the component after mounting, compares that with the target mounting position, and calculates the positional deviation. This allows the system to evaluate mounting accuracy, detect misalignment, and support correction or quality control in the component placement process.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise patent-style description of a unit that can replace a cassette-type feeder and measure mounting position deviation using nozzles, measurement components, and a fiducial mark.
counterfactuals.output:
A replacement measurement unit is configured to be detachably mounted at a feeder mounting position of a component mounting machine in place of a cassette-type feeder. The unit includes a body having an attachment interface corresponding to that of the cassette-type feeder, one or more measurement components held at predetermined positions on the body, and a fiducial mark provided at a known positional relationship with the measurement components.

When the unit is mounted to the component mounting machine, a mounting head equipped with one or more suction nozzles picks up the measurement components from the unit and mounts or positions them at designated measurement locations. An imaging device of the component mounting machine recognizes the fiducial mark to determine a reference position of the unit. Based on the recognized position of the fiducial mark and the detected positions of the measurement components handled by the nozzles, a controller calculates a mounting position deviation associated with the feeder mounting position, the mounting head, and/or the nozzles.

The calculated deviation is used to correct component pickup or mounting coordinates, thereby enabling calibration of the component mounting machine without requiring a cassette-type feeder to be installed.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a patent concerning a component mounting positional deviation amount measurement unit installed in the feeder setting section of a component mounting machine.
counterfactuals.output: An abstract is provided for a component mounting positional deviation amount measurement unit installed in a feeder setting section of a component mounting machine. The measurement unit includes an imaging device and/or position detecting sensor arranged to observe a component held by a mounting head at or near a component pickup position associated with a feeder mounted in the feeder setting section. The unit measures a positional deviation amount of the component relative to a predetermined reference position before the component is mounted on a substrate. A control device calculates correction data based on the measured deviation amount and corrects at least one of a component pickup position, a transfer position, or a mounting position of the mounting head. By locating the measurement unit in the feeder setting section, positional error caused by feeder mounting variation, component supply variation, suction displacement, or nozzle misalignment can be detected promptly without requiring a separate measurement station, thereby improving mounting accuracy while suppressing increases in machine size and cycle time.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe how a measurement unit for a surface-mount component placement machine works, including exchangeable measurement nozzles, measurement components, a mounting table, and a fiducial mark.
counterfactuals.output:
A measurement unit for a surface-mount component placement machine is used to calibrate and verify how accurately the machine can pick up, position, and place components on a board. It typically simulates real placement conditions while providing known reference points for measurement.

The unit includes several key parts:

1. **Mounting table**  
   The mounting table is a stable base or fixture installed in the placement machine. It holds the measurement components in fixed, known positions. The table may be mounted where a printed circuit board would normally be placed, so the machine can perform measurement operations using its normal motion system.

2. **Exchangeable measurement nozzles**  
   The placement head can be fitted with different measurement nozzles. These nozzles are exchangeable so that the unit can test different nozzle sizes, shapes, or pickup conditions corresponding to various component types.  
   A measurement nozzle may include a precisely defined tip, reference geometry, or contact surface. By changing nozzles, the machine can measure placement accuracy under different mechanical configurations.

3. **Measurement components**  
   Measurement components are special test pieces rather than ordinary electronic parts. They may have accurately manufactured shapes, edges, centers, or markings that can be detected by the machine’s camera or measuring system.  
   The placement head picks up a measurement component using the measurement nozzle and places it on, or near, a defined location on the mounting table. The actual position and orientation of the component can then be compared with the intended placement position.

4. **Fiducial mark**  
   A fiducial mark is a precisely located reference mark on the mounting table or measurement fixture. The machine’s vision system uses the fiducial mark to establish the coordinate system of the measurement unit.  
   By detecting the fiducial mark, the placement machine knows exactly where the measurement table is located and can compensate for offsets, rotation, or alignment errors.

In operation, the placement machine first identifies the fiducial mark to align its coordinate system with the measurement unit. A selected measurement nozzle is mounted on the placement head. The nozzle picks up a measurement component and moves it to a target position on the mounting table. The position of the placed component is then measured, often by optical inspection. Any deviation from the expected position indicates placement error, nozzle offset, head alignment error, or calibration drift.

Because the measurement nozzles are exchangeable, the same unit can be used to check multiple placement conditions. This helps calibrate the machine for different component sizes and nozzle types, improving placement accuracy and repeatability in production.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following technical concept into formal patent language: a feeder-replaceable measurement device that lets a mounting head pick up a test component with a measurement nozzle, place it on a table, and measure positional deviation relative to a fiducial mark.
counterfactuals.output:
A feeder-replaceable measurement apparatus for use in a component mounting machine, the component mounting machine including a mounting head configured to detachably hold a nozzle and transfer a component, the measurement apparatus comprising:

a measurement nozzle configured to be attachable to and detachable from the mounting head and to pick up a test component;

a placement table configured to receive the test component placed thereon by the mounting head while the test component is held by the measurement nozzle; and

a fiducial mark provided in a predetermined positional relationship with the placement table,

wherein the measurement apparatus is configured to be mounted to the component mounting machine in a manner replaceable with a component feeder, and

wherein, after the mounting head picks up the test component using the measurement nozzle and places the test component on the placement table, a positional deviation of the placed test component is determined based on a relative position between the test component and the fiducial mark.

In one embodiment, the positional deviation includes at least one of an X-direction deviation, a Y-direction deviation, and a rotational deviation of the test component with respect to a reference placement position defined relative to the fiducial mark. The determined positional deviation may be used for calibration, correction, or verification of pickup accuracy, transfer accuracy, placement accuracy, or nozzle alignment accuracy of the mounting head.
